d:
A short artbook by what appears to have been the J9 F.C., however, the original name of the circle is very grey and unknown as its not listed - the circle states in this particular issue that they would shift their focus to being a Braiger journal instead, thus making it the final issue. A previous book with the same motif was called 'First Revue' but hasn't been located.

On record, this is one of the rarer examples of Gundam doujinshi from the era as several of these works relating to Zeta are exceedingly scarce and hardly go to market. This book features a unique overlay between 0079 and Zeta with illustrations made by high school age girls.

Published and sold at Comiket 29 based on the date it was published and author information.

Additionals:

The mangaka and later animator Yuki Shibata contributed to this imprint when they were in either high school or in college as noted by the colophon and editor.

"Editor's Note:

Thank you very much to our guest, Shibata Yuki. I hope to see you again if the opportunity arises. Thank you also to you and all the other writers. In the future, I will start our club's activities as J9 F.C. It was a short time, but thank you very much. I am in the middle of the manga that was published in First Revue, but I will be suspending it. I'm sorry. I wrote a continuation, but I suddenly scrapped it because I wanted to make the special feature a special feature. I am truly sorry."

The editor appears to have been Jun Sagami (相模潤), who also did the front cover.
